## Publish gate report

**Going out:** Landing page hero, Pebblebrook Tea Co., UK audience.

**Claims check (all on the policy list):**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Loose leaf tea" | Product fact, fine as written |
| "packed by hand in Bristol" | On the list: every tin is packed by hand in Bristol |
| "certified organic by the Soil Association" | On the list |
| "Free UK delivery on orders over £25" | On the list, and the threshold matches |

There are no invented stats, superlatives, guarantees, testimonials or urgency claims.

**Regulated claims:** Organic certification is the only sensitive claim, and the policy backs it. There are no health, money, environmental or price-comparison claims. The "free" delivery has its condition (over £25) stated in the same sentence.

**Disclosure:** This is the brand's own page, with no ad, sponsor, affiliate link, gifted product or AI-labelled content, so no label is needed.

**House style:** The copy is plain and specific, with no AI tells or banned phrases. The one weakness is that "packed by hand in Bristol" appears twice in the first two sentences. I haven't changed it because it doesn't block publication, but you could tighten it to:

> Loose leaf tea, packed by hand in Bristol. Every tin is certified organic by the Soil Association. Free UK delivery on orders over £25.

Check that wording first, though. The Soil Association certification covers the tea, so "our tea is certified organic" is the safer phrasing, and I'd keep it.

**Fixed:** Nothing was changed.

**Needs a decision:** Whether to keep the repeated phrase or use the tightened version. Either is acceptable to publish.

**Approver:** The policy names no approver, so I need an explicit yes from you on the exact final text. Nothing has been published or approved.
